title: Contrasting Two Things: azonban, viszont, ezzel szemben

sections.title: Forming Nuanced Contrasts Between Urban and Rural Realities
sections.content: To contrast two facts, Hungarian uses *azonban* (however), *viszont* (on the other hand) and *ezzel szemben* (in contrast to this). *Azonban* and *viszont* can stand after the first word or phrase of the second sentence; *ezzel szemben* usually opens it. You know *míg* (while, whereas) from Unit 4 for a contrast inside one sentence.

items.spanish: A városban sok a munka. Vidéken azonban csendesebb az élet.
items.english: In the city there is a lot of work. In the countryside, however, life is quieter.

items.spanish: A lakás a városban drága. A faluban viszont olcsóbb a ház.
items.english: A flat in the city is expensive. In the village, on the other hand, a house is cheaper.

items.spanish: A városban sok az ember. Ezzel szemben a faluban kevesen élnek.
items.english: In the city there are many people. In contrast, few people live in the village.
